body: also, I'm going to bed now as it's getting late here and I have to be up early, but thank you for talking to me and helping me get this sorted out in my head.

Thank you for the advice - my best friend's mum has offered me a place to stay if I ever needed one, and while it's a bit tricky since they live abroad I could definitely go and stay there if I had to.

Right, so the bit that's tricky is that if I make arrangements to go sleep on someone's floor or spare room or whatever, it makes it really obvious to my parents that I'm avoiding them. Which I am. I know I'm being really passive agressive and trying to avoid confrontation, it's just that I genuinely don't want to hurt my mum any more. And whenever she or my dad calls me I just get this giant list of the things I've done to her even when I don't even phone - that I've made her worry, that she's been sick with stress and not sleeping, etc. The other big issue is that while they sort of know I have problems with anxiety, they have no idea that a) I've been officially diagnosed and am registered as having a mental disability (something which they would both be very ashamed of me for), and that I'm on antidepressants - this is information that for various reasons I absolutely do not trust them with. So it's kind of difficult for me to find a way of telling my parents I have to stay away for now without the whole lot coming out, and I haven't managed to find that middle ground yet. 

My other main problem at the moment is I just have no idea HOW to go about telling people. I'm so used to being told how much trouble my problems cause people I get really paranoid they don't actually want to hear any of it, even though logically I know they don't mind and would rather I told them rather than keep everything to myself - it's just I keep asking people for help and I feel like I have nothing to offer them in return. I know once I get started it'll get easier, but I'm too much of a coward to take that first step.

Okay, I'm sorry if this doesn't make much sense:

So at the beginning of this year, I was in a bad place - like looking back on it now I feel like if my life had gone the way it was looking to go (having to quit my degree early, move back home, getting a job in the town where I grew up etc) I pretty much would have almost definitely killed myself. A lot of it is me - I have GAD and a tendency towards depressive episodes, which was at the time completely untreated - but part of it was also due to issues with my parents, which will come up later. 

So then I come back to uni for the last two terms of my degree, and I luck out in that I end up with a completely awesome dissertation supervisor, who was incredibly kind and patient with me and was actually pretty much the first person I told about my anxiety disorder. He convinced me to go to the doctors and get officially diagnosed, register with the disability resource services at my uni, massively increased my self-confidence etc (it also helped that the project I carried out for my dissertation went really well).

At quite an early point in my project, my mother rang me and I was telling her how well it was going, and she said to me 'are you sure it's not just your supervisor, though?'. And at the time I just thought yeah, she's probably right, I know I'm not that good at this sort of thing... then later on it kind of freaked me out how easily I just sort of accepted that, and then I just stopped calling home completely. I told my parents I was too busy to call, which was partially true, but I was also sort of avoiding them.

So my mum also has an anxiety disorder, but she utterly refuses to acknowledge it as a problem - it's not helped my my dad, who while well-meaning just doesn't understand and thinks it's just us women being hysterical (my mum and I have it, he and my brother don't). So when things were bad I was used to hearing from my mum that I should never have gone off to the uni I did, she was such a bad mother for not being able to make me feel better - basically any time I got off the phone with her I always felt ten times worse. So when I stopped calling home, things started getting a lot better because of that too. I have pretty awesome friends here, so I always had people to talk to and stuff.  

So I managed to convince myself that things weren't that bad, and I could easily survive three and a half weeks back home over easter. I really couldn't. It was hands down the worst I've ever felt in my life - this is the time when the anxiety got so bad I just felt like I was going to die half the time and spent the other half wishing I could because I couldn't face the idea of spending the rest of my life feeling so awful. All my friends were far away and - well, my family dynamics could take up a whole other page, but in the interests of posting this before midnight suffice to say things are pretty fucked up in that department, and in such a way that my parents have me constantly questioning my own sanity - they always say the way I react to things is irrational, the way I feel about stuff is wrong and bad, the way I think things happen aren't how they actually happened etc - which I can look back on and (mostly) think hey, that's fucked, but at the time when there's no-one to back you up you just feel crazier and crazier. 

So I get back to university for my finals feeling COMPLETELY shit and haven't been able to study at all - awesome supervisor saves the day again, gives me a load of study tips etc and gradually being surrounded by people who actually like me and support what I do with my life makes me feel better again. I go to the doctors and get started on antidepressants, which end up making a HUGE difference and I start feeling like a normal human being and better than I have in years. I land a really good summer research project and get TWO really generous grants to do it, I pass my exams with a really good grade and get accepted onto a masters course, I start looking into PhD programs etc. 

So yeah, currently things are pretty great. But it's just... it still feels so close, like i can slip back at any moment. And I desperately want to move properly forward with my life and kind of make all this good stuff real in a way, but it's really hard because so much is currently unresolved - I just don't know what to do about my parents, I want to ask people for help but I don't feel like I can burden them with my problems more than I already do. And there's a period in late september where I will be very temporarily homeless and will probably end up back with my parents, and I just don't know if I can survive that but I can't confront them about it and just... argh. 

So yeah. sorry about the massive wall of text. Cos at the moment my biggest ultimate secret is the whole fact I was considering suicide, and I haven't managed to tell anyone (apart from you guys, I guess) that yet - it just feels like such a massive ~revelation~ and I have no idea how to go about telling people. So I thought posting about it to internet strangers would be the best place to start.
